To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) decision rules are mapped to ontology binary facts, (2) decision items are mapped to ontology concepts by using the decision binary facts, (3) the decision rules are committed to the mapping results using a pseudo-natural language, (4) the SDTs can be visualized in a scalable manner by using decision binary facts and decision items
the construction process of a Semantic Decision Table is a two-step approach: first, the construction of a rooted tree of facts and then the mapping of decision items to this rooted tree.

the construction of a semantic decision table is possible by building a tree of decision facts and annotating the decision rules with a domain ontology and pseudo-natural language, and that the construction of the semantic decision table is a process that is scalable, flexible and can be performed in a collaborative environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a collaborative decision support tool that helps decision makers to construct and maintain SDTs in a natural manner.
how to construct a SDT in a collaborative environment, and how to visualize it to facilitate the decision process.
a novel way of representing decision tables and their construction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have introduced the concept of Semantic Decision Tables (SDT), and have proposed a methodology to construct them.
the proposed approach provides a novel way for the design of semantic decision tables by means of ontological reasoning.
we present the SDT concept and a method to construct it, which can be applied for any decision making process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach provides a systematic way to construct SDT by using the ontology.
we propose an SDT construction process that allows for the semantic annotation of decision tables and for the formalization of their decision rules.
the proposed approach can help decision makers to better understand the semantic content of the decision table.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SDT is a promising approach for decision support systems.
we have shown that it is feasible to build SDT in an efficient manner.
the use of ontologies can improve the design and management of decision tables.
